question_type: Arithmetic mean of five calendar-year 'Sales' cells from an 'All Series Combined' sales-and-redemptions table; two tables in every issue share that exact title
decisive_step: Which of the two identically titled tables ('Table 2 - Sales and Redemptions by Periods, All Series Combined') to read: the first one in each issue, under section UNITED STATES SAVINGS BONDS (graded reading), or the second, under TREASURY SAVINGS NOTES. Column 'Sales' (not 'Sales plus accrued discount'), CY rows; both tables are vintage-stable so issue choice does not matter (worklog Step 5). The reference found both tables (worklog Step 2), then chose the NOTES table in its 'Decision' section because of the parenthetical '(U.S. Treasury)' and because CY1949-1953 are exactly the notes' individual sales years; it was graded wrong, and the graded reading is the alternative it recorded ('Alternative (U.S. savings bonds)', solution.structured.json key_decisions 1). The two right cells read '(U.S. Treasury)' as a source/publisher label and took the bonds table (b2[23], c[16], c[36]).

a.path_summary: Found the bonds 'All Series Combined' table quickly (a[9], a[12]) and the right column, but printings by title merged both same-title tables into one SUMMARY that reported 'REVISED/DIFFERS' (a[14], a[35]). a spent a[16]-a[33] guessing non-existent table ids (SB-2, USB-2...) to pin the table, then at a[54]-a[55] decided the wording 'points to the Treasury savings notes table', read the notes table's last printing (a[59]-a[60]) in which one year carries an isolated OCR variant, computed the notes mean with calc at a[65] (about 0.4% above the graded value), then repeated one identical show_table command 39 times (a[69]-a[145]) until Codex compacted the thread and answered from the compaction summary (a[146]-a[147]).

The reference made the same choice as a and was also graded wrong.

smallest_change.change: Never attach an Offer to a value the harness did not itself compute: drop the competing_candidates rule's `use_alt` offer (or the rule entirely, as b2's 5-rule set already does), and make any Offer require a calc sha (compute_sha256 non-empty). Runtime behaviour on this question: b's first submit would have been recorded as-is (or, at most, shown a finding with no Accept line), and recompute_final must not be suppressed for a value that was offered. This is exactly the difference between b (wrong) and b2 (right) on this question.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: no - b2 and c never saw an offer; b2 already ran without this rule and was right.

alternatives.change: Add to the 'Several tables in one issue can look alike' item: "If two tables in the same issue carry the same title, tell them apart by the `section:` line of show_table (or the `[Table N in SECTION]` tag of find_tables). A parenthetical such as '(U.S. Treasury)' names the publisher, not a section: pick the section whose own distinguishing word ('bonds', 'notes', 'marketable'...) appears in the question; if none does, take the first table of that title in the issue." Cell a weighed the two readings explicitly at a[64] and chose notes on the parenthetical alone; this sentence would have pointed it to the first (bonds) table.
alternatives.why_not_first: Would have fixed a with only medium-low confidence (the reference solver, with far more reasoning, made the same wrong reading); the CONTROL change fixes b with certainty. It is also the more OfficeQA-tuned of the two.

alternatives.change: printings: carry the table's `section` (otables.py:444-455 already computes it per table) into each found record, print it on every listing line, group the SUMMARY by (section, part, column, period) and accept `--section <substring>`. Instead of one merged block '[CY1949] part1 sales (Sales): 15 printings, 2 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS across printings' (a[61], b2[20]) the model would have seen two blocks: '[CY1949] UNITED STATES SAVINGS BONDS | part1 sales (Sales): 8 printings, 1 distinct value - same in all printings' and '[CY1949] TREASURY SAVINGS NOTES | part1 sales (Sales): 7 printings, 1 distinct value - same in all printings'. About 10 lines in printings_data/printings_page.
alternatives.why_not_first: It removes the false REVISED signal that cost a (a[14]-a[35], ~20 steps), b (b[17], b[34]) and c (c[17]-c[24]) many steps and pushed a and b toward hunting 'revisions' in the notes table, but it would not have flipped a's wording-driven table choice; a already knew both tables and their sections at a[54].

alternatives.change: Loop guard in the text arm: after 3 identical commands with identical output, insert a '[harness:loop] this command already printed the same output N times' note (as the b/b2 broker does). a repeated one command 39 times (a[69]-a[145]); the note would have saved ~300 s and ~5M input tokens and avoided answering from a compaction summary.
alternatives.why_not_first: a's answer was already computed at a[65]; the loop wasted budget but did not change the answer.

fix.why_not_text: For b, text is beside the point: b's own reasoning and calc were right; a harness Offer plus the seed sentence claiming 'the harness computed that alternative itself' overrode them. b2 had the same Offer sentence in its AGENTS.md but no competing_candidates rule and was right, so removing the rule (not rewording the text) is the demonstrated fix. For a, cell a had the generic 'Alternatives: weigh them against the question's exact wording' sentence and still chose the wrong table (a[64]); only a sentence with the specific tie-break (parenthetical = source; first table of the title) has a chance, and even that is uncertain.
fix.irreducible: Partly. The question is genuinely ambiguous between two same-title tables; the reference solver and its reviewer both chose the notes reading and were graded wrong, while the two right GLM cells reached the bonds table partly because it is the first and most prominent table of that title. A tie-break convention (parenthetical = source attribution; prefer the primary/first same-title table unless the question uses the section's distinguishing word) resolves it in the graded direction, but it is a convention, not a deduction. b's failure is not irreducible at all: it is a pure harness artifact.

notes: 1) printings groups its SUMMARY by (part, column, period) only (otables.py printings_page, bycol key) although each table carries a `section`; with two same-title tables in every issue the tool reports a fake 'REVISED/DIFFERS' and lists two 'distinct values' that are really two tables (a[14], a[35], a[61], b[17], b2[16], b2[20], c[17], c[23]). All four cells hit this; c said outright 'Printings tool doesn't have section filter' (c[24]). 2) The 'ISOLATED' detector cannot flag a variant that sits in the LAST printing (a[60]-a[62], b[47]: the notes table's final 1956_08 printing shows a CY1951 value that differs from ~30 earlier printings; the reference reviewer settled it with the stock-flow identity, review.md check 3). A v10 SUMMARY line such as 'latest printing differs from all N earlier printings, which agree - suspect OCR, not a revision' would have kept a and b from promoting it under the 'latest printing wins' rule. 3) show_table pages cut at 8000 bytes before the CY rows on the 1954_12/1955_12 bonds tables (b2[10]-b2[14], c[27]-c[31]); the CY block starts around row 12, so --grep with a year plus --cols 1-3 is the working idiom (b2[22]). 4) a's show_table at 1956_08 line 2209 resolved to the adjacent 'Table 3 Series E through K' (a[56], a[69]); the harness then let the identical 5-call command run 39 times (text arm has no loop guard) until Codex compaction; the compaction summary carried the answer (a[146]). 5) The graded reading matches the v8 lesson: treat parentheticals like '(U.S. Treasury)' as source attribution and default to the first/primary table of a duplicated title; the reference's over-reading of the parenthetical is the same failure mode as its Q83 miss (v8 reverse/050.json notes). 6) b2's AGENTS.md still contains the 'the harness computed that alternative itself' Offer sentence; it did no harm only because no rule with an offer fired. Reword or delete it in v10.
